Merit Employee: Martha R. Buford, 5803 S. Michigan, secretary in the salary administration division of Inland Steel Company, is merit employee of the week. Tear gas in small containers was used by the Cook county sheriff's department to break up a crowd of unruly students at Provisco East high school Friday in Maywood, a suburb of Chicago. The troubles tarted with a feud between white and Negro students in the school's cafeteria and spread outdoors

Dogs held the crowd at bay, but not before one man, identified as Juan Millan, 20 (slumped over), said he was bitten. The disorders broke out in a Latin American neighborhood in Chicago after a man was shot in the leg when a policeman tried to break a gang fight in an alley

Leading march on Capitol: The United Front of Cairo was to march on the Capitol in Springfield today, according to Charles Koen, director, to confront Governor Richard Ogilvie on the tense racial situation in Ciaro. Three clergymen experiencing a weekend of poverty in Chicago took part in a rally at Grant park before a civil rights protest march. Mr. Fischer wore a sweatband around his forehead

A crowd of yelling sign waving teenagers gather in front of Raney High School to listen to a Bible-waving 15 year-old, Bob Thomas as he asks the crowd not to integrate. Little Rock's four High Schools open 8/12, on a partial integration basis, Little Rock, Arkansas
The Selma to Montgomery Marches: police officer watches crowd of marchers. The Dexter Avenue Church, where Martin Luther King Jr was pastor from 1954-1960, is in the background, Montgomery

Anti-war demonstrators use handkerchiefs to cover their faces from blinding tear gas fired at their ranks by National Guardsmen at Michigan and 19th Streets. The Guardsmen used gas to break up a throng of some 5,000 demonstrators attempting to march on the International Amphitheatre, Chicago
Demonstrators outside Conrad Hilton Hotel in Chicago, protesting the Democratic Convention

A young Yippie hangs on to a lamp post and vents his anger at advancing National Guard troops who had been called in to disperse a mob of Yippies. Linked armed demonstrators begin singing songs after they broke police barricades outside the site of the House Un-American activities hearings. About 30 unruly demonstrators stormed the barricades. Paint covers the demonstrators face thrown by an unidentified by-stander, Chicago

Integrationists defying a threat of prosecution threw up picket lines in their second classroom boycott in four months. Happy Demonstrator: One of the demonstrators in protests in East St. Louis, Illinois that erupted into violence almost seems happy as an East St. Louis policeman lifts him from the floor prior to his arrest. Walk Around: Peoria Negros staged a walk around in the Central Illinois Light Company, retail store today seeking prices and information about refrigerators, stoves and various electric appliances. Chicago: This part of a crowd of 3,000 men, women, and children witness the burning of a negro' family's furniture along side of an apartment building in Cicero, Illinois, after teenager broke into the flat and hurled the furniture into the street July 11.
